subject: MAP draft — success signals, exit gates, and escape-hatch plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lane <sarah.lane@veridian.io>, Tom Park <tom.park@veridian.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft — success signals, exit gates, and escape-hatch plan

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I’m attaching a draft Mutual Action Plan that attempts to codify the minimal acceptance signals Veridian needs to feel comfortable moving from trial to purchase, plus a practical set of exit gates and a short escape-hatch (reverse rollout) plan in case we see regressions.

High-level items in the attached MAP:
- Success criteria (functional + performance): token-level latency, end-to-end inference P99, and accuracy/concordance thresholds for the top 3 clinical intents.
- Acceptance tests: smoke run, edge-case coverage, 3-day stability window with live traffic sampling.
- Exit gates: failure thresholds tied to rollback (immediate), canary size limits, and stakeholder sign-off requirements.
- Evidence & owners: test owners, telemetry dashboards, and artifacts required for sign-off.

Ask: please review section 2 (Acceptance Tests) and call out any test coverage gaps by EOD Monday. If this aligns, we’ll lock the MAP and schedule the kickoff for the trial verification week.

Attachments: Veridian_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP matrix), Acceptance_Test_Catalog_v1.pdf (test cases).

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP draft — success signals, exit gates, and escape-hatch plan

Ben —

Big thanks for pulling this together; very helpful framing. Quick questions after an initial pass:
1) For the "concordance" threshold you list 91% for top-3 intents — is that computed on the sanitized Veridian test corpus or live-sampled traffic? We prefer the MAP to reference the corpus used for acceptance.
2) The stability window calls out a 72-hour rolling window — can we add a short warm-up metric to account for cold-start behavior on longer sequences?
3) If rollback is triggered by the canary, what is the expected RTO in your plan (we need an SLA-like expectation for our ops and legal teams).

We’ll review the Acceptance_Test_Catalog with our clinical QA team and get back by Monday.

—Sarah
Sarah Lane
Head of Clinical Product, Veridian Health

Subject: Re: MAP draft — success signals, exit gates, and escape-hatch plan

Sarah / Ben / Tom —

Thanks, Sarah — good calls. A couple of clarifications from Redwood’s side to make the MAP operational for your QA and platform teams:

- Concordance source: we’ll lock the evaluation on the agreed "Veridian-sanitized corpus v1" (see sheet 'data_spec' in the MAP). The live-sampled metric will be a secondary monitoring signal during the 72-hour window.

- Warm-up window: agree to add a 30-minute warm-up bucket for P50/P95 on first-run sequences before we start counting the 72-hour stability window. This reduces noise from initial cold caches.

- RTO / rollback expectation: our operational playbook aims for a 30-minute canary rollback (automated partial route revert) + 2-hour full rollback with on-call runbook. We’ll codify the runbook as an "Escape_Hatch_Playbook.docx" that lists steps, owners and communications templates.

One additional ask from our side: please confirm internal sign-off owners for both Product and Security so we can add them to the MAP sign-off matrix. If you want, I can propose names for the first pass.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben updates the MAP and Test Catalog to reflect the warm-up and corpus source (today).
2) Veridian sends the QA owners + one security contact (by Monday).
3) We lock the MAP and schedule the 72-hour verification run for the week of Aug 24.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Subject: Finalized MAP + acceptance checklist (inc. escape-hatch)

Sarah / Tom —

Following Marissa’s notes I’ve updated the MAP and the Acceptance Test Catalog. Key changes attached and summarized below:

Summary of agreed items:
- Concordance: acceptance measured against Veridian-sanitized corpus v1 (sheet 'data_spec'). Live traffic will be monitored but not gating.
- Warm-up: 30-minute warm-up bucket before the 72-hour stability clock starts.
- Stability window: 72-hour rolling window with zero critical regressions and <1.5% degradation vs baseline on top-3 intent accuracy.
- Canary & rollback: automated canary at 5% traffic for 6 hours, automated partial revert (target RTO 30 mins), full rollback target 2 hours.
- Evidence pack: acceptance requires: (1) test run artifacts (logs + sanitized output samples), (2) telemetry screenshot (P99 latency, error rates), (3) a sign-off email from Veridian Product + Veridian Security.

Timeline proposal:
- Aug 18: Redwood delivers final test harness and runbook.
- Aug 24–26: 72-hour verification run (canary on Aug 24 morning).
- Aug 27: Acceptance review + sign-off or remediation plan.

Attachments: Veridian_MAP_v1.xlsx (updated), Acceptance_Test_Catalog_v1.pdf (updated), Escape_Hatch_Playbook.docx (runbook).

Please reply with QA owners + security contact and confirm the Aug 24 kickoff. If all good, I’ll send a short calendar invite for the kickoff + a readiness pre-check 24 hours prior.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
